segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ לֹא יֹאמַר אָדָם לַחֲבֵירוֹ: הַלְוֵינִי כּוֹר חִטִּין וַאֲנִי אֶתֵּן לָךְ לַגּוֹרֶן. אֲבָל אוֹמֵר לוֹ: הַלְוֵינִי עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא בְּנִי אוֹ עַד שֶׁאֶמְצָא מַפְתֵּחַ. וְהִלֵּל אוֹסֵר. וְכֵן הָיָה הִלֵּל אוֹמֵר: לֹא תַּלְוֶה אִשָּׁה כִּכָּר לַחֲבֶרְתָּהּ עַד שֶׁתַּעֲשֶׂיהָ דָּמִים, שֶׁמָּא יוּקְרוּ חִטִּין, וְנִמְצְאוּ בָּאוֹת לִידֵי רִבִּית.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «A person may not say to another: Lend me a kor of wheat and I will give» it back «to you at» the time the wheat is brought to «the granary,» as the wheat may increase in value, which would mean that when he gives him back a kor of wheat at the time the wheat is brought to the granary it is worth more than the value of the loan, and he therefore will have paid interest. «But he may say to him: Lend me» a kor of wheat for a short period of time, e.g., «until my son comes or until I find» the «key,» as there is no concern about a change in price during such a short interval of time. «And Hillel prohibits» the practice even in this case. «And Hillel would similarly say: A woman may not lend a loaf» of bread «to another unless she establishes its monetary» value, «lest the wheat appreciate» in value before she returns it, «and they will» therefore «have come to» transgress the prohibition of «interest.»
